detailed_description: Word Cloud Generator renders manually weighted terms or simple counts from pasted text. Edit words and weights, load a sample, set the title, choose one of four color themes and five shapes, adjust font sizes and rotation, then export the current preview as PNG or vector SVG. Text generation lowercases input, removes punctuation, splits on whitespace, ignores single-character terms, and keeps up to 100 terms with weights equal to counts multiplied by 10. Separate Chinese words with spaces or edit rows manually: there is no automatic Chinese segmentation, sentiment analysis, document import, batch generation, typeface picker, or custom background-color control.
usage_steps: Start from the sample data or edit the word and weight rows manually.
Optionally paste text into Text Input and click Generate from Text to create weighted terms.
Set the chart title, color theme, shape, font-size range, and rotation range.
Review the live chart preview and adjust terms or weights until the layout is readable.
Download the finished word cloud as PNG or SVG.
usage_examples: Visualize common themes from a short customer-feedback sample.
Create a keyword cloud for a classroom slide or internal workshop.
Turn a list of campaign terms into a quick presentation graphic.
Compare how different weights affect emphasis before exporting a chart.

faqs.question: Can I import a document?
faqs.answer: No. The current page accepts pasted text and manual word rows; it does not include a document import control.

faqs.question: How does Generate from Text work?
faqs.answer: It lowercases text, removes punctuation, splits on whitespace and ignores single-character terms. It keeps up to 100 terms and multiplies each frequency by 10 for the weight. The filter mainly retains English letters, digits, underscores and basic Chinese characters; use manual rows for other scripts. Chinese requires spaces between words.

faqs.question: Which export formats are available?
faqs.answer: PNG is a bitmap. SVG preserves the current shapes and text as vectors rather than embedding a PNG; its text appearance can depend on fonts available on the receiving device.
